To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a glycoprotein purified from buffalo blood, termed as FMSF, promotes motility of caprin caudal sperm cells and its binding efficacy is maturation-dependent and is present on the anterior part of the sperm head.
FMSF is a maturation-dependent motility stimulant that is expressed on the anterior head region of spermatozoa and may have a role in their fertilizing potential.
FMSF is a sperm motility stimulating glycoprotein, which binds to spermatozoa and stimulates their motility in a maturation-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and localization of FMSF-binding receptor in the maturing spermatozoon.
a better understanding of FMSF as a potential marker of sperm maturation and its possible role in fertilization.
the receptor-expression and functional role of FMSF during the maturation process of spermatozoa, and its presence in uterine fluid of cattle species.

FMSF is a maturation-dependent motility stimulating factor and is a promising candidate to be used for in vitro fertilization and artificial insemination procedures.
FMSF is a sperm motility stimulating factor, whose receptor is essential for the forward motility of maturing spermatozoon.
this factor is an important sperm maturation factor and may be of immense use in in vitro fertilization (IVF) technology.

the factor may play a role in the fertilization process.
the FMSF-receptors are expressed in maturing spermatozoon in a sequential manner that coincides with their motility stimulation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
FMSF is a maturation-dependent factor and its expression is essential for normal sperm cell motility.
the receptor for FMSF is present on spermatozoa from cauda epididymis to the uterine fluid and its binding with the sperm surface induces forward motility in maturing spermatozoon.
the FMSF receptor is a potential candidate to monitor the physiological status of spermatozoa during their maturation in epididymis and to assess the quality of the ejaculate.
